title: Did my prayer count?
hook: Did I break my wudu? Did I pray three or four? Here's how to stop second-guessing every prayer.

screens.text: New Muslims often finish a prayer and wonder, "Did that even count?" Usually, yes. Today you get two tools: a rule that quiets doubt, and a simple fix for real mistakes.

**Doubt doesn't cancel what you're sure of.** A man told the Prophet ﷺ he sometimes felt he'd broken his wudu during prayer. The answer: don't leave the prayer unless you hear a sound or notice a smell [Bukhari 137].
bubbles: So if you're sure you made wudu, and only *wonder* whether it broke, you still have it.
Clothes and floors too: clean unless you know otherwise [First Instructions on Worship Part I].

screens.situation: Halfway through Maghrib, Hannah feels a vague "maybe something happened" and wonders if her wudu broke. She heard and smelled nothing.

options.text: Keep praying. Her wudu stands until she's sure it broke
options.feedback: Yes. A maybe doesn't cancel what she's sure of. That's straight from the Prophet's ﷺ guidance.

options.text: Stop, redo wudu, and start over just in case
options.feedback: Not quite. Restarting over a maybe feeds the doubt, and it tends to come back stronger.

options.text: Finish, then repeat the prayer twice to be safe
options.feedback: Not quite. Her prayer counts. Repeating it over a vague feeling isn't required, and it wears you out.

items.text: You made wudu, and now wonder whether it broke
items.why: You still have wudu until you're sure it broke [Bukhari 137].

items.text: A vague feeling mid-prayer, with no sound and no smell
items.why: A maybe doesn't cancel what you're sure of. Keep praying.

items.text: You're not sure a spot on the floor is clean
items.why: Floors and clothes are clean unless you know otherwise.

items.text: You clearly heard yourself pass wind
items.why: That's not doubt; you're sure. Your wudu is broken, so redo it and pray again.

screens.text: **Overthinking has a name: *waswasa*** (nagging doubts, often about wudu and prayer). It loves extra effort: washing again, restarting, repeating. The way out is the opposite: go with what you're sure of, and move on.
bubbles: If doubts are taking over your day, tell {{mentor.name}}. It's common, and it gets better.

screens.prompt: Build the rule that quiets doubt
screens.answer: Doubt doesn't cancel what you're sure of
screens.feedback: That's it. Sure beats maybe, every time [Bukhari 137].

screens.text: **Forgot a required part by mistake?** There's a built-in fix: ***sujud al-sahw*** (the forgetfulness prostration), two extra prostrations near the end of the prayer.
bubbles: It isn't needed for skipping something optional.

screens.title: The forgetfulness prostration
screens.intro: Say you skipped the sitting after the second rak'ah. Keep going. Here's the fix at the end.

moves.text: Carry on with the prayer until its last sitting.
Near the end of the prayer, make two extra prostrations. {{masjid.name}} will show you exactly where they go.
Finish the prayer with the salam. Your mistake is repaired.
In the last sitting, say the tashahhud.
Give **one salam, to the right** only.
Sit, and say the tashahhud again, and what follows it.
Now finish with both salams: right…

screens.prompt: Dre stands up for the third rak'ah of Dhuhr and realizes he skipped the sitting after the second. He's fully standing. What now?

options.text: Keep going, and do the forgetfulness prostration at the end
options.feedback: Right. Once fully standing, carry on. The forgetfulness prostration repairs it.
Not quite. No restart needed. The forgetfulness prostration exists for exactly this.
Not quite. Skipping that sitting by mistake is what the forgetfulness prostration at the end is for.

steps.text: Go with the lower number, because that's the one you're sure of
Finish the prayer from there, then make the forgetfulness prostration [Muslim 571]
A doubt that only comes after you've finished is normally ignored
Is this kind of doubt new for you? End the prayer and pray it again.
Does it happen to you often? Go with what feels most likely. If nothing does, take the lower number
Then finish and make the forgetfulness prostration [Bukhari 401]
A doubt that only comes after the salam is ignored

screens.text: Answer the next doubt with what you're sure of.
steps: Next time a "did that count?" thought shows up, say to yourself: "I'm going with what I'm sure of"
screens.optional_extra: Walk through the forgetfulness prostration once on your prayer mat, outside prayer, so it's familiar.

screens.text: Sure beats maybe: doubt doesn't cancel what you're sure of. For a real mistake, the forgetfulness prostration fixes it.
Allah made the prayer with room for human mistakes. You don't have to be perfect, just present.

prayerPhrase.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ، وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
prayerPhrase.translit: Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa 'ala ali Muhammad, kama sallayta 'ala Ibrahima wa 'ala ali Ibrahim, innaka hamidun majid
prayerPhrase.meaning: O Allah, send Your blessings on Muhammad and his family, as You sent blessings on Ibrahim (Abraham) and his family. You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
prayerPhrase.when: Salat Ibrahimiyya part 1. Only in the last sitting of a prayer, right after the tashahhud. In the middle sitting of a 3- or 4-rak'ah prayer, stop after the tashahhud and stand up. The Prophet ﷺ taught these words [Bukhari 3370].

check.prompt: You're sure you made wudu, but you wonder if it broke. What's the rule?

options.text: You still have wudu until you're sure it broke
options.feedback: Right. Doubt doesn't cancel what you're sure of [Bukhari 137].
Not quite. A maybe doesn't break wudu. Redoing it feeds the doubt.

check.prompt: What is the forgetfulness prostration (sujud al-sahw) for?

options.text: Repairing a required part of the prayer you missed by mistake
options.feedback: Right. Two extra prostrations at the end fix an honest mistake.

options.text: Making up a prayer you missed completely
options.feedback: Not quite. A missed prayer is made up as its own prayer. Sahw fixes mistakes inside a prayer.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Certainty isn't removed by doubt: someone who feels they may have broken wudu in prayer doesn't leave unless there's a sound or smell [Bukhari 137]. Things are pure unless known to be impure [First Instructions on Worship Part I].
- Hanafi sujud al-sahw: due when a **wajib** (required) act is left out by mistake (e.g. the first sitting, the tashahhud, al-Fatiha in a rak'ah where it's due), or done late. Method: after the tashahhud in the last sitting, one salam to the right, two prostrations, sit, repeat the tashahhud, Salat Ibrahimiyya and a du'a, then the two salams [Qibla 34580 (Faraz Rabbani); SeekersGuidance, proofs for the Hanafi method]. Evidence for prostrating after the salam: [Abu Dawud 1038] (hasan) and Ibn Mas'ud's narration [Bukhari 401].
- It isn't performed for deliberate omissions (a deliberately skipped wajib means the prayer should be repeated) or for skipped sunnah acts [Qibla 34580].
- Hanafi doubt about the number of rak'ahs: if this doubt is new to the person, the prayer is invalidated and repeated; if it happens often, act on the strongest impression; if none, build on the lower number and make sujud al-sahw. Doubts after the salam are ignored unless near-certain a rak'ah was missed [Qibla 36786, from *al-Hadiyya al-'Ala'iyya*]. Other schools: build on the lower number and prostrate before the salam [Muslim 571]. (scholar question Q25)
- Forgetting the first sitting (Hanafi): if they're closer to standing (legs straightened) or fully up, they don't go back; they finish and make sujud al-sahw. If they're still closer to sitting, they sit back down, say the tashahhud, and no sahw is due [Qibla 35619; Qibla 43843].
- Prayer phrase: Salat Ibrahimiyya part 1 [Bukhari 3370], in the final sitting only.

**Likely questions**
- *"I keep redoing wudu."* Name it kindly (waswasa), give the rule, suggest one wudu and no repeats for a week, and talk to their mentor. If it's distressing or compulsive, gently mention it can be OCD-like and a counselor can help; that's not a lack of faith.
- *"I forgot a whole prostration / a whole rak'ah."* This is a missed pillar (fard), not just a wajib. In general: if still in the prayer, make it up and do sujud al-sahw; if unsure or already finished and spoke, ask the imam. Keep it short and escalate details.
- *"What counts as required?"* Short Hanafi list: al-Fatiha, a surah in the first two rak'ahs, stillness, the first sitting, the tashahhud, ending with the salam. Don't overload.
- *"Do I need sahw for every little thing?"* No: only a required part missed by mistake, not optional sunnahs.

**Escalate:** a missed fard (prostration, rak'ah); scrupulosity that's disrupting daily life (mentor and, if needed, a counselor); the "first time" doubt question for converts (below).

**Don't**
- Don't encourage repeating prayers or wudu "to be safe."
- Don't make the convert feel their past prayers were invalid.
- Don't overload with the full list of sahw cases.
madhabNote:
- **When the forgetfulness prostration comes:** Shafi'is make it before the salam; Malikis before the salam for something left out and after it for something added; Hanbalis mostly before, with some cases after. Hanafis after one salam (screen 8).
- **Losing count:** the other three schools build on the lower number and prostrate before the salam [Muslim 571]. Hanafis distinguish a first-time doubt from a habitual one, following Ibn Mas'ud's narration to go with one's best judgment [Bukhari 401].
sourcesMd:
- [Bukhari 137](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:137): don't leave the prayer over a feeling unless there's a sound or smell.
- [Muslim 571](https://sunnah.com/muslim:571): unsure of the count, build on what you're sure of, two prostrations.
- [Bukhari 401](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:401): if in doubt, aim for what's correct, complete, then two prostrations.
- [Abu Dawud 1038](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1038) (hasan, al-Albani): two prostrations after the salam for forgetfulness.
- [Bukhari 3370](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3370): the wording of Salat Ibrahimiyya.
- First Instructions on Worship Part I: purity is the default; don't feed doubts.
